newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Four partners in Filipino petrochemical project.
newsitem.headline: Four partners in Filipino petrochemical project.

text.p: Four companies on Wednesday signed an agreement to participate in a 250,000 tonnes a year polyethylene project in the Philippines, Malaysia's national oil firm Petronas said in a statement on Thursday.
The partners are Petronas, BP Holdings International BV, Sumitomo Corp of Japan and Bataan Polyethylene Holdings Corp (BPH).
BPH comprises Filipino companies Profinda, All Asia Capital & Trust Corp and Wellex/Pacific City, which will own a 45 percent interest in the joint venture firm.
BP Holdings will hold a 30 percent stake, Petronas 20 percent and Sumitomo five percent.

The plant in Bataan will be one of the first petrochemical projects in the Philippines to cater to its growing plastic fabrication industry which is currently dependent on imports, the statement said.
Construction of the plant, located about 150 km from Manila, will begin in the third quarter, with operations scheduled to start in the last quarter of 1999.

The joint venture partners and International Finance Corp, a part of the World Bank, will embark on a two-day road show in Malaysia's Labuan island and in Singapore from Thursday (July 10) to syndicate loans for the project. No financial details were given.
